name: Central African Republic
summary: No official Central African guidance on bringing a casket into the Central African Republic was found. Contact the CAR embassy in the country of death before arranging transport to Bangui.
documents: Removal/transport permit from the country of death
coffin: Not published. A hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in an outer wooden case is the international standard; confirm with the embassy.
embalming: Not published for entry; embalming should be expected.
consular: Not published; no CAR embassy page on transfers of remains was found. France's foreign ministry notes that countries outside the Berlin 1937 and Strasbourg 1973 agreements set their own entry conditions and may require non-contagion certificates or embalming, so the consulate's list prevails.
arrival: Customs and health clearance at Bangui M'Poko airport; a local undertaker collects. Temperature-controlled storage exists in Bangui but may not elsewhere.
private_aviation: No published rule specific to private or charter flights was found. A casket on a private aircraft should arrive at an international airport with customs and health (port health) officers, with landing permission arranged through a local handling agent, and the original documents travelling with the casket. Check current security and airspace notices for the CAR with the handling agent.
private_jet_note: Confirm entry documents and Bangui landing arrangements before departure.
export: Documents: hospital medical death certificate (several days, French), civil registry death certificate, certificate of identification and autopsy report from judicial police/prosecutor for sudden or violent deaths, certificate of embalming and transfer permission from local authorities. Few local undertakers can supply international caskets quickly. Release usually within a few days; road deaths can take over a month. No cremation.
export_points: Prosecutor documents for sudden or violent deaths
Few undertakers have international caskets quickly
Release usually within a few days; road deaths can take over a month
No cremation available

Obtain the death certificate, removal permit and medical certificates.
Embalming and sealing of the coffin.

key_points: Entry rules not published officially: confirm with the embassy

name: Congo (Republic)
summary: The embassy of the Republic of Congo issues an 'Authorization for the transfer of human remains' on a file prepared by the funeral home and family (citizenship proof, medical record of death, embalming certificate, funeral home licence, flight reservation). Allow 5 to 7 business days.
documents: Copy of the deceased's birth certificate
Proof of Congolese citizenship (passport, national ID or citizenship certificate)
Hospital medical record certifying the death and its cause
Funeral home letter confirming it handles the shipment to the Republic of Congo
Funeral home certificate that the body was embalmed under local sanitary rules and poses no health threat
Copy of the funeral home's licence
Signed letter from the family representative to the Ambassador, with a copy of their photo ID
Flight reservation or itinerary for the remains
Prepaid tracked return envelope (when applying by mail)
coffin: Not specified by the embassy. A hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in an outer wooden case is the usual international standard; confirm with the embassy and the airline.
embalming: Required: the embassy asks for a funeral home certificate that the body was embalmed and poses no health risk.
consular: The Congolese embassy or consulate in the country of death issues the authorisation for the transfer of human remains. The Washington embassy states 5 to 7 business days from receipt, no express service, payment by money order or cash in person, fees non-refundable. Translators must be recognised by the Congolese authorities. Not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement.
arrival: Arrival clearance at Brazzaville Maya-Maya or Pointe-Noire is not published; a local undertaker collects. No official burial deadline found.
private_aviation: No published rule specific to private or charter flights was found. The embassy asks for the flight reservation or itinerary of the remains, so submit the charter details and confirm acceptance. Land at Brazzaville or Pointe-Noire with customs and health services, with the original documents travelling with the casket.
private_jet_note: The transfer authorisation needs the flight itinerary and takes 5-7 business days: book early.
export: Documents: hospital medical death certificate (several days), civil registry death certificate (French), certificate of identification and autopsy report from judicial police/prosecutor for sudden or violent deaths, certificate of embalming and permit to transfer, arranged through local and international undertakers. Translators must be recognised locally. Release usually within a few days; road deaths can take over a month. Cremation is available.
export_points: Prosecutor documents for sudden or violent deaths
Embalming certificate and transfer permit
Local offices work 07:30-15:30
Cremation available

Embassy processes the authorisation for the transfer of human remains (5-7 business days).

summary: No official Chadian guidance on bringing a casket into Chad was found. Contact the Chadian embassy in the country of death before arranging transport to N'Djamena.
documents: Death certificate (French or Arabic translation if needed)
Removal/transport permit from the country of death
coffin: Not published. A hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in an outer wooden case is the international standard; confirm with the embassy.
embalming: Not published for entry; embalming should be expected.
consular: Not published; no Chadian embassy page on transfers of remains was found (Washington embassy site checked). France's foreign ministry notes that countries outside the Berlin 1937 and Strasbourg 1973 agreements set their own entry conditions and may require non-contagion certificates or embalming, so the consulate's list prevails.
arrival: Customs and health clearance at N'Djamena airport; family or a local undertaker collects. No official burial deadline found; Muslim families usually bury quickly.

Authorities must be told of infectious conditions (e.g. hepatitis, HIV). The passport may be needed for repatriation. Information gathering can be bureaucratic and slow. No cremation in Chad.

name: Gabon
summary: No official Gabonese page on bringing a casket into the country was found. Expect a death certificate, embalming and non-contagious disease certificates, a hermetically sealed casket and legalisation by a Gabonese consulate. Confirm with the consulate.
documents: Certificate that death was not due to a contagious disease
Consular legalisation or authorisation (to be confirmed)
coffin: Not officially published for entry. A hermetically sealed zinc-lined casket in a wooden outer case is the usual standard.
embalming: Not officially published for entry. Usually expected.
consular: Gabonese consulates legalise civil documents; a specific entry transfer permit is not published online (no repatriation page found on the Gabonese embassy sites checked). France's foreign ministry notes that countries outside the Berlin 1937 and Strasbourg 1973 agreements set their own entry conditions and may require non-contagion certificates or embalming, so the consulate's list prevails. Gabon is not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement.
arrival: Not officially published. Collection in Libreville by a Gabonese funeral home. Cremation is not available in Gabon.
private_aviation: No published rule specific to private or charter flights was found. A private aircraft carrying a casket must land at an international airport with customs, immigration and health services; have the local handling agent and receiving funeral home confirm in advance that the remains can be cleared from a private flight.
private_jet_note: Confirm clearance at Libreville Léon-Mba with the handling agent before departure.
export: When a death occurs in Gabon, a funeral home preserves the body and provides a funeral pass, and the Town Hall establishes the death certificate. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Directorate of Consular Affairs) translates the documents. The deceased's consul writes to the Ministry of the Interior, which issues a 'definitive authorization' to transfer the body. Libreville funeral homes stock coffins and containers that meet international standards. Registration can take time. Cremation is not available; the nearest is in Cameroon (Yaounde or Douala).
export_points: Funeral pass from the funeral home, death certificate from the Town Hall
Ministry of the Interior 'definitive authorization' required

No cremation in Gabon

name: Equatorial Guinea
summary: The Equatorial Guinea embassy issues free consular assistance for repatriating a national's remains. Its online application asks for the death certificate, the deceased's passport or ID, an embalming certificate, a non-infectious disease certificate, a hermetically sealed coffin certificate and a burial transit permit.
documents: Original official death certificate issued by the local health authorities
Burial transit permit from the country of death
Funeral home details and flight details (airline, date, route, e.g. Houston-Malabo)
coffin: Hermetically sealed coffin required: the embassy asks for a certificate that the coffin is hermetically sealed. Zinc lining and outer case are not specified; a metal-lined sealed casket in a wooden outer case is the usual standard. Who witnesses the sealing is not published.
embalming: Required: an embalming certificate is a mandatory upload when the family wishes to repatriate the remains.
consular: Apply to the Equatorial Guinea embassy or consulate in the country of death (online application at the Washington embassy). The consular emergency team reviews the death certificate and repatriation authorisations and liaises with the funeral home for transit permits. Service is free. Equatorial Guinea is not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement.
arrival: Clearance procedures at Malabo or Bata are not published. Arrange collection by a local funeral service in advance.
private_aviation: No published rule specific to private or charter flights was found. The embassy form asks for airline, date and route of the repatriation flight, so give the charter operator, date and route instead and confirm with the embassy that a private flight is acceptable. Land at an international airport (Malabo or Bata) with customs, immigration and health services.
private_jet_note: The embassy asks for flight details before authorising; escorts also need visas and yellow fever vaccination.
export: Not officially published. Expect to need a death certificate, embalming and authorisation from the local authorities. Confirm with the consulate of the destination country.
export_points: Exit rules are not officially published
Contact the destination country's consulate early

name: Burundi
summary: No official Burundian guidance on bringing a casket into Burundi was found. Contact the Burundian embassy in the country of death; expect a death certificate, embalming certificate, transfer permit and a special international casket.
documents: Permit to transfer the remains from the country of death
Consular authorisation from the Burundian mission (to be confirmed)
coffin: Not published. UK guidance notes funeral directors use special caskets for the international carriage of human remains; a sealed zinc-lined coffin should be expected.
embalming: Not published for entry; a certificate of embalming is always required for exit, so embalming should be expected.
consular: Not published; the Burundian embassy in Brussels lists no transfer-of-remains procedure online. France's foreign ministry notes that countries outside the Berlin 1937 and Strasbourg 1973 agreements set their own entry conditions and may require non-contagion certificates or embalming, so the consulate's list prevails.
arrival: Customs and health clearance at Bujumbura airport; a local funeral director collects. No official burial deadline found.
private_aviation: No published rule specific to private or charter flights was found. A casket on a private aircraft should arrive at an international airport with customs and health (port health) officers, with landing permission arranged through a local handling agent, and the original documents travelling with the casket.
private_jet_note: Confirm entry documents with the Burundian embassy before departure.
export: A local or international funeral director arranges the local death certificate (French, usually within a day), a certificate of embalming and a certificate permitting transfer of the remains. Local formalities normally take 3 to 4 days for natural deaths; suspicious deaths involve the police and an autopsy report may take up to a month. All hospital bills must be paid before the body is released. No cremation in Burundi (nearest in Rwanda).
